preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10⁴) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for n in [int(line.split()[0])] if len(line.split()) > 0)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵) representing the size of permutation a.

preconditions.expression: all(len(a) == n and all(0 <= x < n and a.count(x) == 1 for x in a) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for a in [list(map(int, line.split()[1:]))] if len(line.split()) > 1)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line contains n distinct integers a₁, a₂, ..., aₙ (0 ≤ aᵢ < n) representing a permutation of integers from 0 to n-1.
The sum of n across all test cases does not exceed 10⁵.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly t lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(line) < 10**9 + 7 for line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: Each output line is a non-negative integer representing the number of similar permutations modulo 10⁹ + 7.

postconditions.expression: all(int(stdout.splitlines()[i]) == count_similar_permutations(a) % (10**9 + 7) for i, line in enumerate(stdin.splitlines()[1:]) for a in [list(map(int, line.split()[1:]))])
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output line is the count of permutations b such that for all intervals [l, r] in a and b, MEX(a[l..r]) == MEX(b[l..r]), modulo 10⁹ + 7. The function count_similar_permutations(a) is defined as the number of such permutations b.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(line) <= 10**5 for line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: The output values are within the feasible range for the problem constraints.
